findings.finding: The 41-row end-stage hall puts a large part of the congregation far from the preacher: 1,261 seats are more than 40 m and 837 more than 45 m from the pulpit, so the rear half depends on IMAG screens to see the preacher's face. Pushing the platform back against the rear wall (PL07) added about 5.85 m to every seat's distance.
findings.evidence: comparison.md: pulpit distance mean 35.52 m, p90 51.42 m, max 57.58 m, rows 41; own measurement from model/blender_manifest.json (ARC-PULPIT at x 29.5, y 71.45 to 3,000 CountsTowardTarget chairs): min 11.08 m, 1,261 > 40 m, 837 > 45 m; basis_of_design.md s.2 'Max eye distance to platform edge 51.3 m'; DESIGN_BRIEF PL07 (5.85 m open floor in front of platform).
findings.fix: Bring the platform forward into the 117 m2 unallocated floor (SP-02F) with a thrust lip, and keep a smaller ministry floor. Better still, test a fanned / wider-shallower bowl, or the floor-plus-balcony option already sketched (about 32-36 m max), to cut the 41 rows to about 30.

findings.finding: Straight, parallel rows in a 49.4 m wide hall make side seats turn their heads a long way: 670 seats turn more than 30 deg (max 52.5 deg) and 156 sit more than 45 deg off the pulpit. A fanned bowl was never studied.
findings.evidence: comparison.md: head turn mean 20.5 deg, max 52.5 deg, 670 seats > 30 deg; open_issues.md OI-19; basis_of_design.md s.4 (A-26: >45 deg 156, worst 52.45 deg).
findings.fix: Curve or angle the rows (rotate the outer blocks by 10-15 deg, or arc the rows about a focus at the platform front) so the chairs face the pulpit. Re-run the C-value rake.

findings.finding: Arrival and departure rely on the upper foyer. Rows 20-41 (about 1,600 people) enter and leave through rear exits at +4.42, then use two foyer stairs (10.8 m total) down to a ground foyer of only 484 m2 plus 225 m2 under the mezzanine. That is about 0.24 m2 per person for 3,000 people, which is tight for the crowds between back-to-back services common in Zimbabwean churches.
findings.evidence: space_schedule.csv SP-05 Main foyer 484.27 m2, SP-06 225.19 m2, SP-07 Upper foyer 377.44 m2; basis_of_design.md s.4 (2 foyer stairs, 10.8 m, risers 0.170); ARC-STAIR-FOYER-E/W; long_section.png (upper foyer +4.42).
findings.fix: Deepen the ground foyer by one bay (8 m) or add side foyers off the ambulatories, so that the arrival hall is about 0.4-0.5 m2 per person. Consider vomitories under the rear rake so the rear rows can reach ground level without the mezzanine.

findings.finding: The sanitary allowance is far too small for 3,000+ occupants: two 34 m2 toilet blocks plus four 16 m2 accessible WCs, with no WCs on the upper foyer. This makes the foyer layout unreliable, because correctly sized toilets would take a lot of foyer area.
findings.evidence: space_schedule.csv SP-WC-W 34.27 m2, SP-WC-E 34.27 m2, SP-WCA-W1/W2/E1/E2 16.39 m2 each; open_issues.md OI-11 (fixture counts not designed). Option B allows 74.34 m2 per block for the same 3,000 seats.
findings.fix: Size the toilet blocks from a provisional fixture ratio (flagged as an assumption pending local code), probably 2-3 times the present area. Place them in side foyers or along the ambulatories so the main foyer does not shrink further.

findings.finding: The 117 m2 floor in front of the platform is still marked 'unallocated'. As an altar-call / ministry floor it is a strength, but it is undeclared and leaves a 5.85 m dead gap between the preacher and the front row.
findings.evidence: space_schedule.csv SP-02F 'Floor in front of platform (unallocated) ... altar call / ministry area?' 117.0 m2; floor_plan.png.
findings.fix: Designate it formally as the altar-call / communion floor, with step-free links to the front cross passage and a portable communion table position. Add a low thrust or steps along the platform front.

findings.finding: The choir in the side wings (386 chairs) faces across the platform in straight rows. It sits at floor level below a 1.00 m platform, so for most of the congregation it is seen side-on and partly hidden. Choir-to-conductor and choir-to-band sightlines are not checked.
findings.evidence: comparison.md choir chairs 386; DESIGN_BRIEF PL06/PL08; floor_plan.png SP-03/SP-04; open_issues.md OI-18; PL07 render 04_interior_from_rear.png (choir barely visible behind front blocks).
findings.fix: Put the wing choir on 2-3 shallow risers stepping up away from the platform, angled about 30 deg towards the congregation. Mark a conductor position on the platform front corner.

findings.finding: The exterior reads as a windowless industrial shed: an 88 m long gabled box with 9.6 m2 of glazing in total. The entrance is a low flat-roofed foyer block with a plain columned canopy, giving no civic or ecclesiastical presence, no daylight to the hall, and nothing marking the front door.
findings.evidence: comparison.md glazing 9.6 m2, external wall 5,824 m2, roof top 18.4 m; renders/PL07-ea0efb2777/01_exterior_aerial.png; manifest ENV-CANOPY-ENTRANCE, only one IfcWindow (WN-BOOTH-VIEW).
findings.fix: Make the entrance gable a glazed or screened frontage. Add controlled clerestory or high-level glazing (with blackout) between trusses, and give the entrance canopy a raised central bay and a cross / identity element. Consider deep overhangs and brise-soleil, which suit the climate.

findings.finding: The interior is dominated by exposed trusses, a blank rear wall and six hanging screens (three delay screens mid-hall). There is no focal architectural treatment behind the platform.
findings.fix: Model a stage-wall feature (cross, timber or acoustic panelling) and a ceiling or acoustic cloud zone over the front half. Check that the delay screens do not cut the view of the main screen from rows 20-30.

findings.finding: No renders exist for the frozen baseline PL08. The latest renders are PL07, so the PL08 stair, ramp and choir-row changes are shown only in drawings.
findings.evidence: designs/A-end-stage/renders/ has folders up to PL07-ea0efb2777, no PL08-590d273e35 folder; DESIGN_BRIEF PL08 entry.
findings.fix: Re-render the PL08 views (01-06 plus a platform close-up) so the review evidence matches the frozen model.

strengths: The plan is clear and rational: an axial sequence from foyer to hall to platform to back of house on a regular grid (A-H x 1-12); the booth (ARC-BOOTH-FLOOR at x 29.5) sits on the centre line; a central aisle on the axis serves processions and altar calls.
All sightlines meet C >= 0.060 / 0.121 m (row_schedule.csv; basis_of_design.md s.3), and no seat lacks a usable view of the pulpit or a screen.
A generous 117 m2 open floor in front of the platform (SP-02F) suits altar calls, praise and dance, and communion.
The largest choir provision of the two options (386 chairs, step-free, in the wings, with a wheelchair choir place each side), with the platform rear kept free for the band.
Single-storey seating with no suspended balcony. The balcony alternative was honestly evaluated and documented (balcony_option_section.png).
Back-of-house rooms (vestry, prayer room, green room, storage, plant) are well placed behind the stage with a 153 m2 corridor.
limitations: Scores cover only architecture (15%), church_functionality (15%) and aesthetics (5%). weighted_score = 1.93 is the partial contribution of these three disciplines (35% of total weight); normalised to 0-10 it is 5.5. The PL08 baseline has no renders, so I judged the visuals from PL07 renders plus PL08 drawings and the manifest. I did not open the .blend or IFC; my measurements are from blender_manifest.json and the CSV schedules. I did not assess the acoustic, AV and sanitary adequacy beyond area allowances. No site, orientation or climate data were available for the facade judgement.
certification_disclaimer: This review is a structured concept-stage QA opinion from an AI reviewer. It is not professional architectural certification, code-compliance verification, fire or accessibility approval, or engineering sign-off. All dimensions in the model are unverified pending review by registered Zimbabwean professionals and the authorities.
